class_name: 否定-強い表現-ハズガナイ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Denies a proposition outright on the strength of the speaker's own reasoning: given what we both know, that cannot be so (寝坊するわけがない). The near-synonym はずがない rests on nameable objective or commonsense grounds, while わけがない carries more subjective conviction. わけがない and わけはない are the everyday shapes, bare わけない is casual, and the unrelated 訳ない ('easy') is a different word.

examples.ruby: 毎朝[まいあさ]五時[ごじ]に起[お]きる姉[あね]が寝坊[ねぼう]するわけがない。
examples.english: My sister is up at five every morning — there's no way she overslept.

examples.ruby: あれだけ材料[ざいりょう]にこだわった料理[りょうり]がまずいわけがない。
examples.english: Food made with ingredients chosen that carefully couldn't possibly taste bad.

examples.ruby: 十年[じゅうねん]も一緒[いっしょ]にいた彼女[かのじょ]が嘘[うそ]をつくわけがない。
examples.english: After ten years together, there's no way she'd lie.

patterns.usage_note: Denies an expectation that the known grounds make untenable: I inspect the machine daily, so it cannot be broken (故障するはずがない). It is the negation of expectational はずだ and the natural choice when you can name the reason you expect otherwise, where the near-synonym わけがない sounds more like personal conviction. Distinct from はずではなかった, which laments that things did not go as planned.

examples.ruby: あんなに練習[れんしゅう]した弟[おとうと]が本番[ほんばん]でしくじるはずがない。
examples.english: After all that practice, there's no way my little brother flubs it on the day.

examples.ruby: 毎日[まいにち]水[みず]をやっているこの鉢[はち]の花[はな]が枯[か]れるはずがない。
examples.english: I water this pot every day, so there's no way the flowers are dying.

examples.ruby: 毎日[まいにち]点検[てんけん]しているのだから、機械[きかい]が故障[こしょう]するはずはない。
examples.english: We inspect it every single day, so there's no way the machine breaks down.

patterns.usage_note: Puts a flat denial in the shape of a question, asserting the opposite of what it asks and expecting no answer: 知るかい, そんな話を信じるかい. Its sibling is the ordinary warm yes-no question, which does want an answer: 元気かい, もう慣れたかい. Rough, masculine and somewhat old-fashioned; Kansai adds な (知るかいな), and もんか carries more emotional refusal.

examples.ruby: そんな都合[つごう]のいい話[はなし]、俺[おれ]が信[しん]じるかい。
examples.english: A story that convenient? As if I'd buy it.

examples.ruby: そんな高[たか]い自転車[じてんしゃ]、今[いま]の俺[おれ]に買[か]えるかい。
examples.english: A bike that pricey? Like I could afford it right now.

examples.ruby: 今[いま]さら謝[あやま]って、あいつが許[ゆる]すかい。
examples.english: Apologize at this point? Like he's going to forgive you.

patterns.usage_note: Asks a question in order to deny it: 誰が従おうか says that no one would, どうして忘れようか that one never could, and no answer is wanted. The sibling lane is the ordinary offer or proposal, shall I or shall we (そろそろ出ようか, 半分持とうか), which is the everyday spoken use. This lane almost always rides on an interrogative such as 誰が or どうして and belongs to essays, speeches, and narration; in conversation the same denial goes to もんか.

examples.ruby: 誰[だれ]がこんな不公平[ふこうへい]な決定[けってい]に従[したが]おうか。
examples.english: Who on earth would go along with a ruling this unfair?

examples.ruby: あの日[ひ]の恩[おん]を、私[わたし]がどうして忘[わす]れようか。
examples.english: How could I ever forget what you did for me that day?

examples.ruby: この道[みち]を選[えら]んだ以上[いじょう]、今[いま]さら何[なに]を恐[おそ]れようか。
examples.english: Having chosen this path, what on earth is there left for me to fear?

patterns.usage_note: Denies something outright by putting it as a rhetorical question, either refusing an act (二度と行くもんか) or rejecting a quality or claim (痛いもんか, 複雑なもんか); it takes a plain verb, an い-adjective, or a な-adjective or noun plus な. The sibling lane asks in earnest what the appropriate course would be (どう説明したものか). Emotional and casual, typical of spoken language; ものですか and もんですか are the politer variants.

examples.ruby: あんな失礼[しつれい]な店[みせ]に、二度[にど]と行[い]くもんか。
examples.english: Set foot in that rude place again? Not a chance.

examples.ruby: あんな子[こ]どもだましの映画[えいが]が怖[こわ]いもんか。
examples.english: A cheap scare like that movie? Not in the least.

examples.ruby: あの人[ひと]の言[い]うことなんて、信用[しんよう]できるものですか。
examples.english: As if anything that man says could be trusted.

patterns.usage_note: Negative conjecture: the speaker judges that something will not happen (今日は雨は降るまい, 今回も失敗するまい), the flat counterpart of ないだろう. The sibling lane is first-person negative resolve, a vow not to act (二度と入るまい, 忘れまいと誓う). Formal and old-fashioned, common in writing and in set phrases like 無理もあるまい and ではあるまいか. Besides a verb's dictionary form it takes nouns and adjectives, through ではあるまい, 高くはあるまい.

examples.ruby: 空[そら]の様子[ようす]では、今日[きょう]は雨[あめ]は降[ふ]るまい。
examples.english: By the look of the sky, we're unlikely to get any rain today.

examples.ruby: 姉[あね]ほどの実力[じつりょく]なら、今回[こんかい]も失敗[しっぱい]するまい。
examples.english: As able as my sister is, she surely won't slip up this time either.

examples.ruby: 一度[いちど]道[みち]に迷[まよ]ったのだから、兄[あに]も今度[こんど]は地図[ちず]を忘[わす]れるまい。
examples.english: Having gotten lost once, my brother surely won't forget the map this time.
